SummaryOfPosition.Summary: The Respondent denies negligence and contends that the clinical presentations were consistent with more common conditions, that appropriate investigations were undertaken, and that earlier diagnosis would not have altered the outcome.

FactsReliedOn.item: The Appellant's initial presentations were consistent with mechanical lower back pain, a common condition.
Appropriate clinical examinations were performed at each consultation.
Red flag symptoms only became apparent at the February 2021 consultation, at which point an urgent MRI was arranged.
The tumour type in question has an unpredictable progression pattern.
Even with earlier diagnosis, the Appellant would likely have required surgery with similar risks.

Contentions.item: The clinical decisions taken were reasonable and in accordance with accepted practice.
The symptoms at the earlier consultations did not mandate MRI investigation.
Even with earlier diagnosis, the outcome would have been the same or similar.
Causation is not established on the balance of probabilities.
